claim: The bench demonstration offered as proof that an energy weapon "cannot affect blue" — a hobby laser scorching yellow, red and green swatches while leaving a blue swatch unmarked — is a real and well-understood property of one specific tool. Hobby engravers use blue diode lasers emitting at roughly 445-455 nanometres. Blue material looks blue because it reflects light in the 440-470 nm band, so a blue laser's beam is largely bounced rather than absorbed and deposits little heat; manufacturers publish this as a known limitation, warning that these machines cannot cut blue, white or clear stock. The effect is a property of matching wavelength to pigment, not a property of energy weapons: it also spares white and mirrored surfaces, and it disappears at any other wavelength. Scott Savitz, a senior engineer at the RAND Corporation, told PolitiFact that "while differently colored items vary in the degree to which they absorb different wavelengths of light … shining a laser on an object will give it energy, regardless of the wavelength of the laser and the color of the object." Fact-checkers going frame by frame through Maui imagery found destroyed blue items — including a blue tarpaulin at Lahaina harbor — alongside surviving items of every other color.

sources.label: PolitiFact, Aug. 24, 2023 — Scott Savitz (RAND Corporation) and Michael Gollner (Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering, UC Berkeley) on lasers, color and how fires spread.

sources.quote: Blue objects reflect only light in the spectrum 440-470nm... a blue laser beam (450nm) means blue and white objects reflect the laser light best, while black objects absorb it best.

sources.label: Darkly Labs, acrylic cutting notes — blue acrylic reflects the 445-455 nm beam back rather than absorbing it.

notes: Backstage. The demo footage is genuine and the physics in it is genuine — that is the point of the record, and it is why this is not written as a debunk. Reverse-image search resolves the swatch clip to a YouTube upload titled 'Blue DEW laser fire proof' circulating in DEW compilations; there is no independent lab attached to it, so the record cites the underlying optics from laser-cutter manufacturers rather than the clip. The self-defeating part is left for the reader rather than stated: a 450 nm weapon that spares blue would equally spare white and glass, and could not melt aluminium wheels. Group A on the optics; the inference from it is Group B. RAND/PolitiFact quote verified against the live page.
